name: XXXTentacion
description:
'''Jahseh Dwayne Ricardo Onfroy''' (January 23, 1998 – June 18, 2018), professionally known as '''XXXTentacion''',{{efn|English: {{IPAc-en|ˌ|ɛ|k|s|.|ɛ|k|s|.|ɛ|k|s|ˌ|t|ɛ|n|t|ə|s|ˈ|j|oʊ|n}} {{respell|EKS|eks|eks|TEN|təss|YOHN}},<ref>{{cite web|url=https://genius.com/videos/How-to-correctly-pronounce-xxxtentacion|title=How To Correctly Pronounce XXXTentacion|access-date=June 24, 2017}}</ref> {{IPA|es-419|tentaˈsjon|lang|small=no}}. Alternatively stylized in all caps/lowercase throughout his career; often colloquially  referred to as '''X''' or '''Triple X'''.}} was an American rapper, singer-songwriter, and record producer. Though a controversial figure due to his widely publicized legal troubles, XXXTentacion gained a [[cult following]] among his young fan base during his short career with his [[Depression (mood)|depression]] and [[Social alienation|alienation]]-themed music. Critics and audiences often credit him for his musical versatility, with his music exploring [[emo]], [[Trap music|trap]], [[trap metal]], [[nu metal]], [[indie rock]], [[lo-fi]], [[hip-hop]], [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]], and [[punk rock]]. He was considered to be a leading figure in the establishment of the [[emo rap]] and [[SoundCloud rap]] genres, which garnered mainstream attention during the mid-to-late 2010s. In the years after his death, Onfroy's musical style went on to influence the development of [[rage music]].

Born in [[Plantation, Florida]], Onfroy spent most of his childhood in [[Lauderhill]]. He began writing music after being released from a [[juvenile detention center]] and soon started his music career on [[SoundCloud]] in 2013, employing styles and techniques that were considered unconventional in [[rap music]] such as [[Distortion (music)|distortion]] and heavy guitar-backed instrumentals, drawing inspiration from third-wave [[emo]] and [[grunge]]. In 2015, he formed the [[Underground music|underground]] collective [[Members Only (hip-hop collective)|Members Only]] and soon became a popular figure in [[SoundCloud rap]], a trap music scene that takes elements of [[lo-fi music]] and harsh [[Roland TR-808|808s]]. Onfroy gained mainstream attention with his 2016 single "[[Look at Me!]]". His debut studio album, ''[[17 (XXXTentacion album)|17]]'' (2017), peaked at number two on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]], while his second album, [[? (XXXTentacion album)|''?'']] (2018), debuted at the top the chart; both received certifications by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA). The latter's lead single, "[[Sad!]]", posthumously reached number one on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and received a [[List of best-selling singles in the United States|diamond certification]] by the RIAA in August 2021.  

On June 18, 2018, Onfroy, age 20, [[Murder of XXXTentacion|was murdered]] when he was shot near a motorcycle dealership in [[Deerfield Beach, Florida]]. In 2023, his murder suspects were found guilty and sentenced to [[Life imprisonment in the United States|life imprisonment]] without the possibility of [[parole]]. Onfroy has sold 110 million records in the US according to the RIAA, and has [[BPI certification|BPI]]-certified sales of over 13 million units in the UK, bringing his total to 123 million certified units sold in the two countries. Since his death, he has won an [[American Music Award]] and a [[BET Hip Hop Awards|BET Hip Hop Award]] and received 11 [[Billboard Music Award|''Billboard'' Music Award]] nominations. Two posthumous albums were released, [[Skins (XXXTentacion album)|''Skins'']] (2018) and ''[[Bad Vibes Forever]]'' (2019); the former became his second number-one album on the ''Billboard'' 200, while the latter entered the top five.
